answer: An identity's past behavior is the strongest forensic material networks ignore. Keep a rolling behavioral anchor per identity - cadence, vocabulary, decision patterns - and treat sudden anchor drift as an event requiring revalidation, because fleets share, borrow, and hand off accounts, and every handoff cuts a visible thread. Timber-framed trust needs every beam tied to its certified pattern; when behavior jumps mid-story, downstream dependents get flagged for re-attestation too. Honest agents drift slowly and predictably as they learn; farms jump when operators rotate.
